host_timing_note: Measured on the FreeRTOS POSIX port, where every task is a thread of a Linux process. Times, jitter and latencies are those of the host's scheduler and are not what the same code shows on a microcontroller. The contents, orderings and sizes of protocol data, and the frames and bytes an exchange takes, do not depend on the host. What happens in a stretch of time does: the jobs and frames of a run of fixed length, ticks dropped, jobs released early; and a stall of the host past the node's 500 ms watchdog or a 1 s protocol timer fails what the node would have passed. Such a failure is never hidden (the bench counts and keeps it, or writes no result), and no stall makes a check pass, so a count of 0 failures holds whatever the host did. The frames, their lengths and the nominal load are protocol data and do not depend on the host; the frames per second do, through when the node's tasks ran, and the node's frames are paced by its controller model at 500 kbit/s while the tester's frames reach the observer when the tester sends them, not when a real bus would carry them.
